subject: mathematics
question_text: For any x ∈ R, prove that sinh⁻¹x = logₑ(x + √(x² + 1)).

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the formula or definition you use and how you finish.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Form the quadratic in eʸ
steps.margin_note: First mark. Put y = Sinh⁻¹x so that x = sinh y, write the definition, then multiply by eʸ to clear e⁻ʸ. What is left is a quadratic in eʸ.
steps.memory_tip: Multiplying by eʸ turns eʸ − e⁻ʸ into e²ʸ − 1, which is what makes it a quadratic in eʸ.
lines: Let y = Sinh⁻¹x, so x = sinh y

recall.must_convey: That y = Sinh⁻¹x is set so x = sinh y, and multiplying by eʸ gives the quadratic e²ʸ − 2x·eʸ − 1 = 0.

multiply by e to the y to clear the negative power
you get e to the two y minus two x e to the y minus one equals zero

steps.why: e⁻ʸ is the only thing stopping this from being a quadratic. Multiplying by eʸ removes it and turns the equation into one the quadratic formula solves.
common_mistakes: Multiplying only one side by eʸ.
Writing eʸ·e⁻ʸ as e⁻ʸ² instead of 1.

steps.label: Take the positive root
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Both roots come out of the formula, but eʸ is always positive and x − √(x² + 1) is always negative, so only the plus root survives.
steps.memory_tip: √(x² + 1) is bigger than x for every real x, so x − √(x² + 1) is negative and cannot equal eʸ.

recall.must_convey: That the quadratic gives eʸ = x ± √(x² + 1), the minus root is rejected because eʸ is positive, and taking logarithms gives the result.
accept: the quadratic formula gives x plus or minus root x squared plus one
the minus root is negative and e to the y is always positive so reject it
take logarithms to get log of x plus root x squared plus one
minus root negative untundi so reject chesi log teesukovali
so sinh inverse x is log of x plus root x squared plus one

steps.why: x + √(x² + 1) is positive for every real x, so the logarithm is defined for every real x. That is why the formula holds on the whole of R with no restriction.
common_mistakes: Keeping both roots and writing logₑ(x ± √(x² + 1)).
Choosing the minus root, whose logarithm does not exist.
